title: Wide cross-platform discovery pass 40
summary: Personally review broad cross-platform discovery: add 36 source-backed projects and record four explicit non-promotions.
notes: Root personally ran 52 broad searches, returning 585 hits and 582 distinct repository URLs; 40 selected roots including the canonical CPC upstream were reviewed. No discovery worker was used. Search coverage spans classic computers, consoles, games, disassemblies, decompilations, source archives, language tools, emulators, hardware tests, media tools and filesystem tooling. Coverage is broad, not an assertion that every project was exhausted. Source tree, README, implementation and selected fork comparisons were inspected; no upstream code was executed. Ingestion findings: search token collisions (BBC Micro versus micro:bit); documentation-only forks and renamed-owner links; explicit broken historical sources remain valuable without runnable claims; model inference/MCP/agent configuration must not imply development-AI authorship; format/container limits and source/target CPU direction must survive ingestion. Large GitHub Contents API responses can return empty content without isError: blob fallback recovered seven large catalogue files; such empty results must not mean missing evidence. Used a connector-pinned current catalogue snapshot after shell Git access failed; no stale checkout used for duplicate decisions. Local dry-run uses current catalogue/audit/source/decision snapshots with an older unchanged activity file because the 14 MB current activity blob exceeds the connector fetch limit; repository CI/application must validate against the live activity file before publication is considered complete.

sources.reason: Game-agnostic extraction of instruments from SWIV, Turrican II and Superfrog projects. ADF/HUNK readers, checksum-aware unpackers, conservative 68000 walking, MCP and capture comparison are implemented. Recompiler is explicitly a prototype with a restricted blitter/custom-chip model; unmodelled accesses are logged, not proof of a complete native game port.
Reads and writes DSK/EDSK through the Linux floppy-controller interface. Standard and some unusual geometries are documented; faithful recreation of every protection scheme remains future work.
Historical Z80 syntax checks, vasm symbol extraction and additional graphics/sound helpers. The regex checker explicitly is incomplete, not a full assembler frontend.

Archived educational static-analysis collection of DOS-era specimens. The author describes removing destructive disk-overwrite code, so these are modified analytical listings, not byte-exact original binaries. No specimen was assembled or executed.

Converts planar four-bit cursor images to/from PNG, with splitting/consolidation that preserves unknown leading header data. Travel Junction is the primary target; Pia Carrot MOUSE.DAT is additionally documented.
Queries and changes Human68k DOS console, IOCS display and GraphicMask settings. Source explicitly selects .cpu 68000.
Error-diffusion conversion respects Oric 240×200 graphics attributes and emits TAP with an optional BASIC loader plus BMP preview. Runs as GrafX2 script or command-line Lua.

Inspects/extracts CMD groups, modifies groups and converts flat/H86 input. The 8080 model name is a CP/M-86 loading model, not proof of an 8080 target CPU. exe2cmd is specifically constrained to a Personal CP/M-86 BDOS small-model image, not a general DOS application converter.
A callable 6809 single-instruction decoder with pointer-based string output, not an interactive host disassembly suite.
BRR encoder/decoder and SPC sample extraction, with resampling, loop handling and optional Gaussian filtering. PS1 audio support appears only as a future plan.

Native sound-sequence tests exercise tone, envelope, sweep, waveform, noise and terminal routing. Implemented channel routines provide timed register sequences; this is a test input suite, not an emulator implementation or independently validated fidelity result.
Source expands the sparse README: mapping/DPLC tools, artwork splitting/recoloring, FM voice handling and SMPS-to-assembly conversion are present.
Recovered host-side ADPCM encoding/decoding and codebook/table-design sources. The visible tree does not represent every SDK developer tool, nor a Nintendo 64 game decompilation.
Work-in-progress matching C reconstruction with game-state implementation and asset recovery. Upstream explicitly warns that hardcoded addresses limit shiftability and large-scale mods.
Combines component P/S/M/V/C ROM files into NeoSD .neo containers with metadata. Exotic images including Bad Apple and possibly SS5 Perfect are documented exceptions.
Translation patch materials include script/font extraction, assembly modifications and disc reconstruction. Honorifics flag also selects original versus translated images.

Converts multiple chip/music formats into SAP-R and low-overhead POKEY playback. It explicitly does not make POKEY an exact SID/AY emulator; timer-driven effects, digidrums and rapid envelopes have limits.
Maintained continuation of Torsten Jager fat95 3.18 for FAT12/16/32, with MBR/GPT integration. A filesystem handler is distinct from the required low-level device driver.
Historical font editor port now edits PSF-style VGA-console fonts through curses. Source and README preserve Atari ST ancestry, but current code is not advertised as an Atari executable.
Native screen editor with machine-specific terminal/input adaptations. Text is kept in available TPA; functionality can be configured out to conserve space.
Original PAL source made readable/buildable with xa65. Mixed BASIC/assembly and relocatable output are separate flavours, not simultaneous features.

Annotated engine relocated to RAM, with optional Sargon 2.1 CP/M opening-book replacement. Source explains the original missing book-table byte and changed RESTORE behaviour; this is not an unchanged cartridge reconstruction.
Redirects existing AppleShare FST traffic through TCP/IP rather than replacing the FST. AFP 2.0/optional 2.2 compatibility is explicit; AFP 3.x-only servers are unsupported.

Preserves scans, OCR article and typed BASIC compiler listings from 1985. Maintainer explicitly reports failure even on a small BORDER example and suspects transcription or original-listing errors; working tape version remains missing.
Views/extracts Theme Park floppy/CD sprites, palettes, animation and sound resources. Music playback is explicitly experimental.

Small source-only header inspector prints magic, table pointers, entry address and name. Direct indexing/name scanning lacks a clear malformed-input bounds guard, so it is not a robust universal dump validator.
WAV decoding/encoding, raw-program conversion and BASIC listing with documented cassette format and debug-wave diagnostics.
General multi-system emulator rather than a game-specific emulation port. Source has Z80, 6502, VDP and sound components; guest machines share hardware but have individual media and BIOS constraints.
Inspects/edits RTI instruments and builds RMT banks through a real tracker-driver/emulated-6502/POKEY chain. Source describes working copies and explicit bank saves rather than overwriting originals.
C# library models PRG memory, bookmarks, characters and assembler/disassembler operations, with a related sprite editor. It is not a complete C64 emulator.
libfuse/ADFlib filesystem for OFS/FFS volumes. Defaults to read-write; read-only requires -o ro. Single-thread operation is enforced because concurrent writes can corrupt images.
Wraps m68k-linux-gnu-gcc-8 assembly output and custom gas68k assembler to produce TOS PRG files. It cannot link multiple object files; source inclusion is the documented workaround.

Translates CHIP-8 opcodes to Z80 ROM plus runtime, with ACIA text rendering of the 64×32 display. Translation direction is CHIP-8→Z80, not Z80→host; shipped game inputs do not prove full compatibility.

Interpreted Lisp implementation includes evaluation, reading, printing and mark/sweep GC. README marks tail calls/GC done but notes no string type and inadequate error handling; compilation examples are incomplete.

Manual address/data permutation and bounded heuristic Auto-Fix for scrambled EPROMs. Auto-Fix is explicitly Z80-only despite additional decoder modules; known wiring patterns are tried before general search. Confidence threshold is described as uncalibrated, not proof of universal recovery.
Library/CLI for CoCo DECB virtual disks, file extraction/insertion and formatting. It says JVC format but explicitly neither creates nor recognises a JVC header.
GitHub comparison with already tracked moralrecordings upstream is identical: zero ahead, zero behind. No distinct implementation to add.
Compared with BackupTheBerlios/dsktools: one added README commit only, no code changes. Promote original source archive once.
False platform match: ARM JIT for BBC micro:bit, not the 6502 BBC Micro. module.json names microbit dependencies.

Generic screenshot translation pipeline rather than PC-98 binary/format restoration. Backend uses local Qwen inference and hardcoded local paths; README references absent requirements files. AI inference is not evidence of AI-authored implementation. Retain only as a lead until a distinct preservation/development role is established.
